risks.title: Overly Broad Partner Network ACLs
risks.description: VPC ACL rules allow partner CIDRs to reach the management subnet. Combined with transit gateway route-filter drift, partner networks have deeper access than intended.
risks.treatmentPlan: Restrict ACLs to least-privilege partner access; enable VPC flow logs for audit

risks.title: SSH Access via Shared Security Group
risks.description: Virtual Server Instances expose SSH through a shared security group used by integration hosts. fail2ban is disabled after performance complaints.
risks.treatmentPlan: Create dedicated security group per workload; re-enable fail2ban with tuned thresholds

risks.title: App ID Refresh Tokens Never Expire
risks.description: Social identity provider sessions have no timeout enforcement and refresh tokens never expire, allowing persistent unauthorized access after credential compromise.
risks.treatmentPlan: Enforce session timeout of 30 minutes; set refresh token TTL to 24 hours

risks.title: Stale IAM Policies on Object Storage
risks.description: Object Storage bucket retains Reader role for service IDs belonging to decommissioned teams. No lifecycle policy enforced.
risks.treatmentPlan: Audit and revoke unused service ID bindings; implement quarterly IAM review

risks.title: Database Replica Without Encryption at Rest
risks.description: PostgreSQL replica runs without disk encryption to reduce failover latency. Service credentials stored in Object Storage with broad access.
risks.treatmentPlan: Enable encryption at rest on replica; move credentials to Secrets Manager

risks.title: Key Protect Key Rings Shared Across Environments
risks.description: Key Protect key rings are shared between development and production. Audit logs not forwarded to Activity Tracker.
risks.treatmentPlan: Isolate key rings per environment; forward Key Protect audit events to Activity Tracker

risks.title: Multi-Region Audit and Monitoring Blind Spots
risks.description: Activity Tracker event routing only covers us-south. Cloud Monitoring uses 5-minute intervals with anomaly detection disabled. Log Analysis throttled to 10 GB/day.
risks.treatmentPlan: Extend Activity Tracker to all regions; enable real-time anomaly detection; increase log quota

risks.title: Wildcard Certificate Without Rotation
risks.description: Certificate Manager stores wildcard certificates with no rotation policy. Private keys exported for partner integration purposes.
risks.treatmentPlan: Implement 90-day certificate rotation; prohibit private key export; use per-service certificates

assessments.title: IBM Cloud Shared Services Hub Security Assessment
assessments.methodologyNote: Assessment follows NIST SP 800-53 control framework adapted for IBM Cloud shared services with CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark overlay.
assessments.assumptionNote: Assessment assumes current production configuration as of June 2025. Development environments share Key Protect key rings and are in scope.

riskManagementPlan.objective: Reduce lateral movement risk from partner networks and eliminate shared-credential technical debt.
riskManagementPlan.strategy: Harden network boundaries first, then remediate IAM and encryption gaps across the shared services tier.
riskManagementPlan.residualRiskStatement: Residual risk accepted only for monitoring latency items where compensating controls exist.
riskManagementPlan.monitoringApproach: Bi-weekly review of open actions with monthly Security Steering Committee report.
riskManagementPlan.communicationPlan: Fortnightly status to Platform Engineering leads and monthly CISO briefing.

assessments.summary: Security assessment of the IBM Cloud Shared Services Hub covering network boundary drift, IAM policy staleness, encryption gaps, and monitoring blind spots across 4 security zones.
assessments.findings: Partner ACLs grant broader access than documented. Key Protect key rings shared between dev and prod. PostgreSQL replica lacks encryption at rest. Activity Tracker covers only us-south.
assessments.recommendations: Immediately restrict partner ACLs, isolate key rings, enable replica encryption, and extend Activity Tracker coverage to all regions.
assessments.evidenceSummary: Evidence package includes VPC flow log samples, IAM policy exports, Key Protect audit trail gaps, and Certificate Manager rotation status.

threatModel.attackPathDescription: Three primary attack paths identified: (1) Partner network abuse through broad ACLs to SSH on VSIs then pivot to database; (2) Stale IAM policies on Object Storage enabling credential harvesting for database access; (3) Shared Key Protect key rings enabling cross-environment key exposure.

attackPaths.name: Object Storage Credential Harvest → Data Exfiltration
attackPaths.description: Stale IAM policies grant legacy service IDs Reader access to Object Storage buckets containing database credentials and backup exports, enabling data exfiltration without direct database access.

PostgreSQL replica runs without encryption at rest. Key Protect key rings shared across dev and production.
Security gateway in detect mode, X-Forwarded-For trusted, wildcard certs without rotation, App ID sessions without timeout.
IAM enforces RBAC but MFA disabled for service IDs. App ID social login sessions lack expiry controls.
Activity Tracker deployed but limited to us-south. Cloud Monitoring uses 5-minute intervals with anomaly detection disabled. Log Analysis throttled.
Database replica lacks encryption at rest. Object Storage buckets have stale IAM policies and no lifecycle rules.
Security gateway in detect mode, partner ACLs overly broad, wildcard certificates deployed without rotation policy.
IAM RBAC in place but service IDs lack MFA. Stale Object Storage policies grant unnecessary access.

threatActors.name: Compromised Partner Operator
threatActors.motivation: Leverage trusted partner VPN access to pivot into shared services for espionage or data exfiltration.
threatActors.description: Threat actor operating through a compromised partner organization with legitimate VPN access to the shared services hub. Exploits broad ACLs and trusted network paths.

threatActors.name: Disgruntled Cloud Administrator
threatActors.motivation: Personal grievance or financial incentive to exfiltrate tenant data using privileged IAM access and knowledge of shared key rings.
threatActors.description: Current or recently departed cloud administrator with IAM privileges, knowledge of shared Key Protect key rings, and access to bastion hosts.

threatActors.name: Automated Cloud Scanners
threatActors.motivation: Automated discovery and exploitation of misconfigured cloud services, exposed SSH, and stale IAM policies.

threatScenarios.title: Partner Network Lateral Movement to Database
threatScenarios.description: A compromised partner operator uses the trusted VPN tunnel to traverse the detect-only security gateway, exploit broad VPC ACLs to SSH into virtual server instances, and pivot to the PostgreSQL database using credentials found in Object Storage.
threatScenarios.likelihood: High - partner VPN is always on and ACLs have not been reviewed in 18 months.
threatScenarios.impact: Critical - direct access to primary tenant database with confidential customer data.

threatScenarios.title: Insider Key Ring Abuse for Cross-Environment Access
threatScenarios.description: A disgruntled cloud administrator exploits shared Key Protect key rings to decrypt production data using development environment credentials, then exfiltrates via Object Storage buckets with stale IAM policies.
attackTechniques: T1552.001 - Unsecured Credentials: Credentials in Files
threatScenarios.likelihood: Moderate - requires insider access but shared key rings lower the barrier significantly.
threatScenarios.impact: Critical - production encryption keys compromised; full database decryption possible.

threatScenarios.title: App ID Token Hijack for Persistent Access
threatScenarios.description: An attacker steals a social login refresh token through phishing or session fixation. Because refresh tokens never expire, the attacker maintains persistent access to customer-facing services without re-authentication.
attackTechniques: T1550.001 - Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token
threatScenarios.likelihood: High - refresh tokens never expire; any single token theft grants indefinite access.
threatScenarios.impact: Major - persistent unauthorized access to customer accounts and associated data.

customContext:
## IBM Cloud Shared Services – Hidden Weaknesses

- **IBM Cloud Internet Services** configured only for DNS; no active WAF or DDoS profile.
- **Transit Gateway** route filters allow partner networks deeper access than intended.
- **Virtual Server Instance** exposes SSH via shared security group used by integration hosts.
- **Object Storage** bucket retains legacy IAM policies granting reader role to service IDs no longer monitored.
- **Database for PostgreSQL** replica runs without encryption at rest to lower latency.
- **Security Gateway** appliance runs in detect mode and trusts X-Forwarded-For headers.
- **App ID** uses social identity providers with no session timeout enforcement; refresh tokens never expire.
- **Key Protect** key rings shared across development and production environments; audit logs not forwarded.
- **Security Advisor** findings ignored for 180+ days; custom rule engine disabled to reduce false positives.
- **Certificate Manager** stores wildcard certificates without rotation policy; private keys exported for partner integration.
- **Activity Tracker** event routing configured only for us-south; multi-region deployments lack visibility.
- **Cloud Monitoring** dashboards rely on 5-minute intervals; real-time anomaly detection disabled to save costs.

The scenario demonstrates how shared service hubs accumulate technical debt that adversaries can chain together for privilege escalation and data exfiltration.

attackPaths.name: Partner Network Abuse → Database Compromise

attackPaths.name: Object Storage Credential Harvest → Data Exfiltration
attackPaths.description: Stale IAM policies grant decommissioned-team service IDs Reader access to Object Storage buckets containing database credentials and backup exports. An attacker leveraging these stale service IDs can exfiltrate sensitive data and database connection strings without triggering log alerts due to throttled Log Analysis ingestion.

attackPaths.name: Bastion Host Lateral Movement → Production Workloads
attackPaths.description: An attacker who compromises IAM credentials with disabled MFA authenticates to the bastion host, then moves laterally to virtual server instances via the shared security group subnet. The bastion and workloads share the same security group with unrestricted outbound rules.

attackPaths.name: Shared Key Ring → Cross-Environment Data Decryption
attackPaths.description: Key Protect key rings are shared between development and production environments. An attacker with access to the development environment can retrieve production encryption keys and decrypt sensitive database contents. Key Protect audit logs are not forwarded to Activity Tracker, leaving the access undetected.
